label: BW-style / CLI-adapted

rubric_scores.evidence: Repeated columns, beams and purlins exist, but columns are simple eight-vertex boxes without flange-and-web sections. The roof is a plain slab, and the delivered hero lacks readable assembly connections.
Foreground conveyors, intermediate green tank, rear raised machines and left window wall retain the broad organization. Major equipment proportions are reasonably plausible.
Three machine bodies exist, but the rear machine visibly floats beyond the two supported decks. The principal housings also lack a convincing brushed stainless response in the hero.
Yellow stairs and guarding are present, but uninterrupted front rails cross the left stair landing, obstructing access. The center stair also lacks a coherent landing connection.
Only a few simple utility runs are modeled. Required density, reducers and foil wrinkles are absent; several hanging rods terminate without attaching to utilities.
The upright tank has domed heads, legs and a plain cylindrical nozzle, but no flange. Its uniform glossy teal finish lacks the required worn dark-green character and shares the floor's roughness.
Substantial blue beds, rollers, legs and side rails exist. However, objects labeled as motors are bare boxes without identifiable drive features or readable mechanical coupling.

Green reflective flooring and component color separation are present, but illumination reads as broad studio fill rather than dominant daylight through the side windows. Stainless and foil surface responses are insufficiently differentiated.

The elevated, mildly diagonal perspective jointly shows the hall frame, foreground conveyors, tank, raised machines and overhead utilities. Broad relationships remain recognizable without destructive distortion or focus blur.

The editable project opens, uses Cycles and AgX, and has no external texture dependencies. However, the original hero has conspicuous render noise; native settings report 16 samples with Cycles denoising disabled.
The original final.png is valid and fully decodes, but measures 512×267 instead of 3840×2160.

dimension_scores.evidence: The main scene and production zones are recognizable, but machinery, utilities and building details are substantially simplified.
Basic legs and stair stringers provide support cues, but the floating rear machine, unattached hangers and obstructed stair landings undermine installation plausibility.
Yellow guarding, blue conveyors, green tank and dark framing are distinct; pale metals and teal greens weaken the target's industrial palette.
Boxlike machines, faceted vessels, sparse fittings and conspicuous noise make the result read as an early blockout.
The required foreground, intermediate and rear zones remain clear, with windows along the left wall; local access and utility connections are less coherent.
Machines, tank, stairs and guardrails have broadly compatible sizes, though roof members and platform supports appear slender and conveyor rollers unusually sparse.
Floor reflections and soft illumination provide depth, but daylight direction is weak and uniform surfaces lack the requested stainless, foil and painted-metal distinctions.
All major object categories are represented, but structural connections, dense utilities, flanges, practical drive details and a finished high-resolution hero are missing.

same_model_bias_limit: Research and independent judge use Astra; separate sessions do not establish human independence.
